title: How do you map training to compliance obligations?
description: How to trace each compliance obligation to the roles it affects, the learning outcome it needs, the training that delivers it and the evidence that proves it.
shortAnswer: Training is mapped to compliance obligations by breaking each obligation in the obligations register into its people requirements, identifying the roles that must meet each one, writing a learning outcome for each role and requirement, linking the training and assessment that deliver it, and recording the trace so any obligation can be followed forward to evidence and any course followed back to the obligation that justifies it.
keyTakeaways: The unit of mapping is an obligation broken into what a person must know or do, not a whole Act or a whole course.
Not every obligation needs training. Map only those with a people element, and record why the others are handled by systems or controls.
Every mapping row should run obligation, role, learning outcome, training asset, assessment evidence.
The trace must work in both directions: from obligation to evidence, and from course back to obligation.
Regulators such as AUSTRAC and ASIC expect training to be matched to role and risk, which a role level map demonstrates directly.

sections.heading: Why map training to compliance obligations?

blocks.text: Mapping lets an organisation show which obligations its training covers, for whom, and with what evidence. Without it, a training catalogue can only show what was delivered, not whether the obligations that matter were addressed.

Regulators increasingly frame training expectations by role and risk. AUSTRAC guidance on the reformed AML/CTF regime says training must be tailored so that it is appropriate to the person, their role, their responsibilities and the money laundering and terrorism financing risks relevant to that role ([AUSTRAC](https://www.austrac.gov.au/about-us/amlctf-reform/reforms-guidance/amlctf-program-reform/personnel-due-diligence-and-training-reform/amlctf-training-reform)). ASIC's RG 104 expects licensees to identify the knowledge and skills representatives need and to keep a record of the training they have undertaken ([ASIC](https://asic.gov.au/regulatory-resources/find-a-document/regulatory-guides/rg-104-afs-licensing-meeting-the-general-obligations/)). A map is the simplest way to show both.

ISO 37301:2021, the international standard for compliance management systems, lists identifying compliance obligations and personnel training among the measures a compliance management system includes ([ISO TC 309](https://committee.iso.org/files/live/sites/tc309/files/FAQ%2037301/ISO%2037301%20FAQs,%20May%202022.pdf)). A training map connects those two parts of the system.

sections.heading: What are the steps to map training to obligations?

blocks.text: There are seven steps. The work is front loaded: once the obligations are broken down correctly, the rest is disciplined record keeping.

items: **Start from the obligations register.** Use the organisation's [compliance obligations register](/glossary/compliance-obligations-register) as the master list, with each obligation's source, section and version. If no register exists, build the in scope part of one first. Output: the list of obligations in scope with citations.

**Decompose each obligation into requirements.** Split a broad obligation into the specific things that must happen. 'Report suspicious matters' becomes: recognise indicators, escalate internally, decide whether to report, submit within the required time, keep records. Output: an atomic requirement list, each with a parent obligation.

**Classify each requirement.** Decide whether meeting it depends on a person's knowledge, skill or behaviour, or is met by a system, control or contract. Only the first group is mapped to training, but record the reason for the classification of the second. Output: a people requirements list and a controls list.

**Identify affected roles.** For each people requirement, list the roles that perform or oversee it, including contractors and third parties where they perform the function. Output: a requirement by role matrix.

**Write a learning outcome per role and requirement.** State what that role must be able to do, at the depth that role needs. A customer facing consultant and a compliance officer touch the same obligation at very different depths. Output: [measurable learning outcomes](/guides/how-to-write-measurable-learning-outcomes) linked to requirement and role.

**Link training assets and assessment evidence.** Record which module, procedure briefing or on the job activity delivers each outcome, and what evidence shows it was achieved. Output: the completed map.

**Set maintenance triggers.** Record the source version for each obligation and define what happens when it changes: which outcomes, assets and assessments must be reviewed. Output: a change procedure tied to the map (see [updating training when regulations change](/guides/how-to-update-training-when-regulations-change)).

sections.heading: What does a compliance training map look like?

blocks.text: A compliance training map is a table with one row per requirement and role. The rows below are an illustrative sample for a hypothetical financial services business. The obligation citations are real; the roles, outcomes and evidence are examples of how an organisation might express them.

blocks.caption: Illustrative obligation to evidence map
head: Obligation (source)
Role
Learning outcome
Assessment evidence
rows: Provide AML/CTF training tailored to role and ML/TF risk (AML/CTF Act s26F(4)(e), per AUSTRAC guidance)
Identify indicators of suspicious activity in a customer interaction and escalate using the internal procedure
Scenario assessment with scored escalation decisions
Apply enhanced due diligence measures proportionate to customer risk, including source of funds checks, and document the rationale
Review of completed case files against a checklist
Ensure representatives are adequately trained and competent (Corporations Act s912A(1)(f), RG 104)
Explain the product features and the limits of general advice to a customer without giving personal advice
Observed or recorded call assessed against criteria
Provide information, training, instruction and supervision necessary for health and safety (model WHS Act primary duty)
Operate the assigned plant only within the conditions set by the safe work procedure
Practical observation plus confirmation of any required licence

blocks.text: The fourth row draws on Safe Work Australia's statement that the primary duty requires a person conducting a business or undertaking to ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, the provision of instruction, training, information and supervision ([Safe Work Australia](https://www.safeworkaustralia.gov.au/law-and-regulation/duties-under-whs-laws/duties-pcbu)).

sections.heading: How detailed should the map be?

blocks.text: Detailed enough that an auditor can pick any obligation and see who is trained on it, to what outcome, and with what evidence, without a conversation. Coarser than that and the map cannot answer the question it exists for.

items: **Too coarse:** 'AML/CTF Act mapped to AML Awareness course'. This shows no role differentiation and no evidence.
**About right:** one row per atomic requirement per role group, with a named outcome and evidence type.
**Too fine:** a row per paragraph of guidance per individual. Individual status belongs in the [training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix), not the obligation map.

sections.heading: How do you check a compliance training map is complete?

blocks.text: Run four checks in both directions. Each finding goes into the [training gap analysis](/guides/how-to-run-a-training-gap-analysis).

items: Every people requirement has at least one role mapped (no orphan obligations).
Every role mapped has an outcome and an evidence type (no untested coverage).
Every training asset maps back to at least one requirement (no unjustified content, which is a candidate for retirement).
Every obligation's source version matches the current version (no stale mappings).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry holds obligations, roles, concepts, learning outcomes and assessment points as linked records, so the trace from obligation to evidence exists before content is written rather than being reconstructed for an audit. See [audit evidence](/platform/audit-evidence).

faqs.q: Should every compliance obligation have training attached?
faqs.a: No. Many obligations are met by systems, controls, contracts or a small specialist team. Training should be mapped where meeting the obligation depends on people's knowledge, skill or behaviour. Record the reasoning for obligations you do not map, because an auditor may ask why.

faqs.q: Who should maintain the obligation to training map?
faqs.a: Compliance should own the obligations and their interpretation; L&D should own the outcomes, assets and assessments. The map works best as a shared record with both owners named against the columns they are accountable for, and a joint review when either side changes.

A spreadsheet works for a small scope. It becomes hard to maintain once obligations, roles and assets number in the hundreds, because the same outcome appears in many rows and version changes must be applied by hand. At that point a relational or graph based record is easier to keep accurate.

faqs.q: What is the difference between this map and a training matrix?
faqs.a: The obligation map shows why training exists and what it must achieve, at role level. A training matrix shows which people have completed or been assessed on each requirement. The map drives the matrix: the matrix columns should come from the map.
